content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To cite in apa with no author, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Identify the document title (2 minutes)
Step 2. Check for a group or corporate author (5 minutes)
Step 3. Verify the publication year (3 minutes)
Step 4. Determine the source type like a webpage or book (4 minutes)
Step 5. Locate the website name (2 minutes)
Step 6. Format the title in sentence case (3 minutes)
Step 7. Check for a specific edition number (4 minutes)
Step 8. Confirm the URL is active (1 minute)
Step 9. Identify the day and month for newspaper sources (2 minutes)
Step 10. Scan the document for any editor names (6 minutes)
Step 11. Check the copyright page for missing details (5 minutes)
Step 12. Review the APA manual for specific no-author rules (10 minutes)
Step 13. Place the title in the author position of the reference (2 minutes)
Step 14. Note the volume and issue numbers (3 minutes)
Step 15. Search for a Digital Object Identifier (8 minutes)
Step 16. Verify the italicization rules for the title (4 minutes)
Step 17. Finalize the full reference entry (5 minutes)
Step 18. Look for a retrieval date if the content is dynamic (5 minutes)
Step 19. Open a new document for the bibliography (1 minute)
Step 20. Alphabetize the entry by the first significant word (6 minutes)
Step 21. Set the document margins to one inch (2 minutes)
Step 22. Cross-reference the title with the in-text citation (7 minutes)
Step 23. Check if "Anonymous" is explicitly used as the author (3 minutes)
Step 24. Verify the punctuation between elements (4 minutes)
Step 25. Check for double spacing (1 minute)
Step 26. Note the publisher's name (3 minutes)
Step 27. Ensure the year is in parentheses (2 minutes)
Step 28. Locate the physical or digital copy of the work (15 minutes)
Step 29. Check for a translator if applicable (5 minutes)
Step 30. Confirm if the work is part of a larger series (4 minutes)
Step 31. Identify the page range for articles (3 minutes)
Step 32. Shorten the title for the in-text citation (5 minutes)
Step 33. Italicize the journal name if necessary (2 minutes)
Step 34. Check for special characters in the title (1 minute)
Step 35. Proofread the entire reference list (10 minutes)
Step 36. Apply hanging indents (2 minutes)
Step 37. Download a citation management tool (15 minutes)
Step 38. Verify the location of the publisher (4 minutes)
Step 39. Check for consistency across all citations (12 minutes)
Step 40. Look for a DOI on the landing page (5 minutes)
Step 41. Export the citation to a text file (2 minutes)
Step 42. Compare the entry against a sample paper (8 minutes)
Step 43. Search for the source in a library database (10 minutes)
Step 44. Draft the bibliographic entry (6 minutes)
Step 45. Check for proper capitalization of proper nouns (3 minutes)
Step 46. Look for a stable permalink (4 minutes)
Step 47. Gather all available metadata (20 minutes)
Step 48. Determine if the source is a blog post (3 minutes)
Step 49. Check for a publication city (3 minutes)
Step 50. Verify that the title is not a proper noun (4 minutes)
Step 51. Check the 7th edition updates (10 minutes)
Step 52. Ensure the font is Times New Roman (1 minute)
Step 53. Confirm the corporate author isn't the publisher (5 minutes)
Step 54. Identify the database name (3 minutes)
Step 55. Look for an archive URL (6 minutes)
Step 56. Format the publisher information (4 minutes)
Step 57. Check for a subtitle (3 minutes)
Step 58. Look for a report number (5 minutes)
Step 59. Double check the URL formatting (2 minutes)
Step 60. Check for a specific paragraph number for quotes (4 minutes)
Step 61. Review the list for duplicate entries (5 minutes)
Step 62. Search for a DOI in a global registry (10 minutes)
Step 63. Capitalize the first letter of the first word (2 minutes)
Step 64. Place a period at the end of the entry (1 minute)
Step 65. Verify the volume number formatting (3 minutes)
Step 66. Check for a DOI prefix (2 minutes)
Step 67. Identify the source language (4 minutes)
Step 68. Verify the alphabetical order in the list (5 minutes)
Step 69. Confirm the publication state or country (4 minutes)
Step 70. Search for a publication timestamp (5 minutes)
Step 71. Check for a Creative Commons license (3 minutes)
Step 72. Identify the medium of the source (5 minutes)
Step 73. Search the library catalog (15 minutes)
Step 74. Check for a print version of the source (8 minutes)
Step 75. Ensure the title is exactly as it appears (5 minutes)
Step 76. Review the reference for extra spaces (2 minutes)
Step 77. Check the citation for a specific video timestamp (4 minutes)
Step 78. Verify the issue number is in parentheses (2 minutes)
Step 79. Search for an original publication date (7 minutes)
Step 80. Review the final citation for typos (5 minutes)
